source.firm: Granite Island Group (Gloucester, MA; founded 1987; president/senior engineer James M. Atkinson)
source.expansion: TSCM = Technical Surveillance Counter Measures (the firm's own expansion of the acronym)

pages.title: Technical Surveillance Threat Levels and Defensive Countermeasures
Sequence of Events for a TSCM Inspection
Background and Qualifications - James M. Atkinson

source.note: Paraphrased distillation of Granite Island Group's published defensive doctrine, for defensive inspection planning only. Nothing here describes how to build, place, or operate an eavesdropping device; the source pages' offensive-detail material is deliberately not reproduced.

principles: Secure contact first: never discuss a suspected compromise over a suspect phone, cordless, or cellular link; meet away from the suspect facility.
Escalate silently: passive, non-alerting inspection phases precede any activity that could alert an eavesdropper; each phase only runs if the threat model justifies its cost.
Detection difficulty rises roughly an order of magnitude per threat level (Granite's levels 1-9), so the inspection level must be matched to the adversary class, not to budget habit.

An inspection always covers the full emanations picture: RF from 20 Hz to above 110 GHz, light spectra 250 nm to 1750 nm, all wiring (AC, telecom, LAN, HVAC, alarm), imaging equipment, and phone lines verified back to the central office.
If a device is found: stop, document, preserve forensically, and notify law enforcement where appropriate - do not simply remove and discard the evidence.

threatClusters.actors: Spouses, curious amateurs; consumer toys and gadgets not designed for eavesdropping (wireless mics, intercoms, baby monitors, Wavecom transmitters)
threatClusters.profile: Mostly below 1 GHz (49 MHz, 88-108, 143, 171, 470, 900-925 MHz), under 50 mW, AM/NFM/WFM, high harmonic content; infrared clustered near 900 nm

threatClusters.actors: Private investigators, spy shops, advanced amateurs; quasi-consumer broadcast/ham/maritime gear misused for surveillance
threatClusters.profile: Broadcast UHF/VHF wireless microphones, industrial wireless video, 2.4 GHz ISM spread spectrum; phone-line devices still betray parasitic power draw on a meter test

threatClusters.actors: Law-enforcement and professional eavesdroppers; the typical threat for corporate offices
threatClusters.profile: Devices engineered for surveillance: conducted (carrier-current/VLF on wiring), PBX and voicemail compromises, laser and infrared optical paths
threatClusters.kitBenchmarkUsd: spectrum analysis to 40 GHz-class, telephone analyser, time-domain reflectometer

threatClusters.actors: Diplomatic, intelligence, and state-level adversaries; defence contractors, aerospace, law firms at the top of the risk scale
threatClusters.profile: Long-term, high-risk technical surveillance designed to defeat inspection; burst, hopping, and stored-and-forward exfiltration
threatClusters.kitBenchmarkUsd: at least $750,000 in TSCM equipment at the top level (spectrum/vector analysers DC-40 GHz, NLJD, portable X-ray, TDR)

threatClusters.actors: Emerging technologies - and claimed threats based on misunderstanding or fantasy, which Granite explicitly separates from real levels
threatClusters.profile: Assess against physics first; a large share of reported 'impossible' surveillance resolves to ordinary emanations or error
threatClusters.kitBenchmarkUsd: threat-model review before any instrument is unpacked

phases.title: Client initiates secure contact
checks: Contact made away from the suspect facility, never over a suspect telephone/cordless/cellular link
Background materials on the facility sent to the TSCM firm
Secure face-to-face meeting arranged if requested

phases.title: Initial meeting and commissioning
checks: Sterile meeting location away from the facility
Client concerns and vulnerabilities discussed
Plan agreed in advance for the event a device or hazard is found
Services commissioned if appropriate

phases.title: Pre-inspection survey and reconnaissance
checks: Facility blueprints reviewed
External RF survey (9 kHz to 26.5/40 GHz)
Facility exterior reconnaissance

phases.title: Vulnerability analysis
checks: Threat assessment and threat model developed
Physical and electronic security assessments
Internal RF survey
Communications systems and facilities audited
Sensitive areas, intercept locations, and probable listening posts identified
Structural elements (walls, ceilings, floors) evaluated; furnishings inventoried

phases.title: Silent / passive walk-through
checks: Non-alerting activity only - nothing to tip off an eavesdropper
Automated bug and wireless-microphone detection (9 kHz to 3 GHz)
Initial VLF inspection of AC, telecom, LAN, and HVAC wiring
Infrared/laser, video camera, recorder, and ultrasonic detection
Catches most PI, spy-shop, and amateur devices (~4 h for a brief walk-through)

phases.title: Passive RF and light spectrum monitoring
checks: Full passive RF spectrum sweep (20 Hz to above 110 GHz)
Full passive light spectrum sweep (300 nm to 1710 nm)
Ambient cover maintained (music, normal phone use, drapes pulled)
Catches advanced amateur devices

phases.title: Active inspection - non-alerting
checks: VLF/RF checks on AC mains at outlets, switches, fixtures; HVAC, alarm, fire sensors
All phone lines evaluated and traced back to the central office
Telephone sets, PBX (hardware and software), and voicemail checked for modification
Computer, LAN, printer, and imaging-device inspection
Forensic light sweeps (UV under 400 nm, IR above 700 nm, tuned sources 250-1750 nm)
Oblique-light and wallplate/baseboard inspection
Catches law-enforcement and professional devices; typical corporate threat level

phases.title: Active scan - alerting
checks: Chirp detection of hidden microphones and transducers
IR/audio/ultrasonic countermeasure jamming as required; device rendered temporarily inoperative
Furnishings, ceilings, walls, and HVAC ducts opened and inspected
Thermal and acoustical-leakage inspection
Borescope inspection of wallplates and electrical boxes
Catches professional devices; typical for Fortune 500 offices and law firms

phases.title: Active scan - alerting / evaluation
checks: TDR/FEXT/NEXT verification and tracing of every conductor class (telephone, LAN, CCTV, AC mains, HVAC, alarm, fire)
PBX/ESS translations and voicemail evaluated
Copier and fax inspection; PBX/alarm/HVAC security verified
Wall, floor, and ceiling cavity inspection - every cubic centimetre
Catches diplomatic, law-enforcement, and intelligence devices; typical for attorneys, defence contractors, aerospace

phases.title: Special inspection activities (as needed)
checks: Non-linear junction detector (NLJD) inspection, active and passive - finds electronics whether or not they transmit
X-ray, radiographic, and fluoroscope inspection
Magnetic anomaly inspection

phases.title: Preventive actions (special request only)
checks: Cavities, wallplates, and artifacts sealed and dusted for tamper evidence
Acoustic, ultrasonic, IR, and RF countermeasure 'cloaks' installed as needed
In-place monitoring (IPM) alarms installed
Encryption devices, high-security locks, doors, and hinges installed
Client education and training

phases.title: Post-inspection activities
checks: Verbal presentation of findings before leaving the site
Hard-copy report if requested
Corrective and follow-up actions agreed
Recurring TSCM service scheduled if the threat model warrants it

phases.title: If an eavesdropping device or activity is detected
checks: Document the device or activity in place - collection before disturbance
Notify law-enforcement agencies if appropriate
Forensic identification and analysis of the device
Counter-surveillance and counter-intelligence follow-up

generalParameters: Analysis of all RF/electromagnetic emanations from 20 Hz to above 110 GHz
Active and passive light spectra examined from 250 nm to 1750 nm
All outlets, switches, and lighting inspected for VLF/RF devices
All PBX, LAN, WAN connections and equipment inspected; computers audited for security anomalies
All copier, fax, and imaging equipment inspected; fibre-optic connections and cabling inspected
All phone lines inspected and verified back to the central office
All locks, safes, and physical security devices evaluated
